verdict.rationale: Loops documents event-triggered email workflows (onboarding, activation, upgrade, winback) that are set up once and then run automatically, and those workflow graphs can be created and published from code. Coverage is limited to lifecycle email sequences started by events, with no documented recurring schedules or general background agent jobs. missing for 10: documented time-based or recurring schedule triggers, automation beyond email workflows, details on monitoring or run history of background automations, independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can set up automations that run autonomously in the background

citations.quote: Reach users after they close the tab. Set up onboarding, activation, upgrade, and winback emails once, then improve them over time.
Create and update workflow graphs, change mailing lists, and add, branch, edit, or delete nodes from code. Send events to start published workflows.
Build onboarding, trial, and re-engagement workflows around your product events.
POST /events/send Send an event to trigger workflows
